ref_extractions.title: A Multilingual Handwriting Learning System for Visually Impaired People
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes a voice-over guided handwriting learning system for visually impaired people using image processing and Random Forest ML. It does not involve EEG recording, neuroimaging analysis, or use of any OpenNeuro dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: ML classification of handwriting images, not EEG data.

ref_extractions.title: Wearable Assistive Tactile Communication Interface Based on Integrated Touch Sensors and Actuators
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper presents hardware design of a wearable tactile glove for finger Braille communication. It is an engineering/hardware paper with user testing but no EEG neuroimaging component and does not use any EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Hardware design paper, no EEG or neuroimaging analysis.

ref_extractions.title: Haptic artificial muscle skin for extended reality
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes development of haptic DEA actuators for XR skin-integrated interfaces. It is a materials science/engineering paper with no EEG analysis and does not use any OpenNeuro dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Materials engineering paper on haptic actuators, no EEG data used.

ref_extractions.title: UbiBraille: designing and evaluating a vibrotactile Braille-reading device
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper presents design and user studies of a vibrotactile Braille-reading device. It involves human experiments but uses behavioral accuracy measures, not EEG neuroimaging, and does not use any OpenNeuro EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: HCI device paper with behavioral user studies, no EEG neuroimaging.

ref_extractions.title: Feeling form: the neural basis of haptic shape perception
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a neurophysiology review paper about tactile shape perception including Braille as an example. It discusses neural coding but does not present original EEG/fMRI data, does not use the openneuro_ds004951 dataset, and does not define any ML classification task on EEG.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper on tactile neural coding, no dataset usage.

ref_extractions.title: Brain–Computer Interface Spellers: A Review
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article about BCI spelling paradigms (P300, SSVEP, MI). It discusses EEG-based BCI systems generally but does not use or reference the openneuro_ds004951 dataset, nor does it apply ML classification to this specific dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review article about BCI spellers, no specific dataset used.

ref_extractions.title: Human–Machine Interaction through Advanced Haptic Sensors: A Piezoelectric Sensory Glove with Edge Machine Learning for Gesture and Object Recognition
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper presents a piezoelectric sensory glove for gesture recognition using ML on sensor signals. It is about wearable haptics/ML classification of hand gestures from glove sensors, not EEG-based classification of Braille letter perception from brain signals.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Wearable sensor/ML paper, EEG not involved.

ref_extractions.title: The transformation of sensory to perceptual braille letter representations in the visually deprived brain
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses EEG and fMRI to study Braille letter representations in blind participants with multivariate classification, which is thematically related to the dataset paradigm. The shared EEG domain and Braille letter classification task make it partially relevant.

tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Braille Letter Identity Classification (8-class)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.1 s, tmax = 0.999 s, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S 1` | 0 | Braille letter B |
  | `Stimulus/S 2` | 1 | Braille letter C |
  | `Stimulus/S 3` | 2 | Braille letter D |
  | `Stimulus/S 4` | 3 | Braille letter L |
  | `Stimulus/S 5` | 4 | Braille letter M |
  | `Stimulus/S 6` | 5 | Braille letter N |
  | `Stimulus/S 7` | 6 | Braille letter V |
  | `Stimulus/S 8` | 7 | Braille letter Z |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.7554/eLife.98148
  - DOI: 10.7554/eLife.98148.2
- **Kernel Notes**: Per the source study, 8 Braille letters (B, C, D, L, M, N, V, Z) were classified using SVM with cross-hand transfer learning. E and O were excluded as vigilance targets. Baseline correction: -100ms to 0ms. The source study used N=11 blind participants; ds004951 contains N=23 (sighted controls + congenitally blind). Mapping S1-S8 to specific letters requires verification from ds004951 documentation. Exclude S9-S16, S101/S222 (feedback markers), S200 (block boundaries), and S253-S255 (admin markers).

### Normal Task 1: Braille Letter Identification (16-class)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S 1` | 0 | Braille letter 1 |
  | `Stimulus/S 2` | 1 | Braille letter 2 |
  | `Stimulus/S 3` | 2 | Braille letter 3 |
  | `Stimulus/S 4` | 3 | Braille letter 4 |
  | `Stimulus/S 5` | 4 | Braille letter 5 |
  | `Stimulus/S 6` | 5 | Braille letter 6 |
  | `Stimulus/S 7` | 6 | Braille letter 7 |
  | `Stimulus/S 8` | 7 | Braille letter 8 |
  | `Stimulus/S 9` | 8 | Braille letter 9 |
  | `Stimulus/S 10` | 9 | Braille letter 10 |
  | `Stimulus/S 11` | 10 | Braille letter 11 |
  | `Stimulus/S 12` | 11 | Braille letter 12 |
  | `Stimulus/S 13` | 12 | Braille letter 13 |
  | `Stimulus/S 14` | 13 | Braille letter 14 |
  | `Stimulus/S 15` | 14 | Braille letter 15 |
  | `Stimulus/S 16` | 15 | Braille letter 16 |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.7554/eLife.98148
- **Kernel Notes**: The 16-class variant captures all Braille letter stimulus events (S1-S16) for a comprehensive classification model. The extended window (-0.2s to 1.0s) is recommended for comprehensive tactile processing coverage. Exclude S101/S222 (~63k each, feedback/block markers), S200 (~10k, block boundaries), and S253-S255 (admin markers). This task is distinct from the 8-class task which targets specific letters analyzed in the source study.
